previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with multiple comorbidities, including morbid obesity, COPD, congestive heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted after being found confused and hypoxic at her nursing home. She presented with altered mental status, hypoxia, and signs of acute heart failure with pulmonary edema. Workup revealed an ESBL-producing E. coli urinary tract infection and cellulitis of a recent skin graft site on her right leg. Her acute kidney injury, with creatinine rising to 3.9, was attributed to pre-renal causes and resolved with supportive care. She was treated with IV diuresis for heart failure and IV meropenem, later transitioned to outpatient ertapenem via a PICC line for a two-week course. Her mental status improved with correction of hypoxia and infection. She was discharged to extended care with plans for wound care, IV antibiotics, and follow-up with her primary care provider for anticoagulation evaluation and PICC removal.
